home.title: Home
home.kicker: Software engineer, PhD in computer graphics
home.lead: Seventeen projects, about fifteen languages, one common thread: 3D meshes and their topology. Each project is generated with AI, then reviewed, tested and documented by me.
home.thread.title: The common thread
home.thread.text: One mesh runs through the whole portfolio: read in C, analysed in C++, served by Python, Java and C# APIs, classified by an ML model, stored in SQL and displayed in React, Angular and Qt.
home.genai.title: Generated by AI, reviewed by a human
home.genai.text: The code is written with Claude Code. My added value: the specification, a review of every diff, the tests and a blocking CI. Each project has a REVIEW.md file listing the AI mistakes I fixed.

demo.title: Try lib-c in your browser
demo.lead: The file is read by the C library compiled to WebAssembly: it never leaves your browser.
demo.choose: Choose an OBJ or PLY file
demo.noscript: The demo needs JavaScript and WebAssembly.
demo.label.euler: Euler characteristic χ = V − E + F
demo.label.genus: Closed surface: if connected and orientable, it has genus g = {g}, since χ = 2 − 2g.
demo.label.open: Surface with boundary: {b} edges belong to a single triangle.
demo.label.closed.other: Closed surface, but χ = {euler} matches no connected orientable surface.
demo.label.error.2: not enough memory for this mesh.
demo.label.error.4: a face refers to a missing vertex.
demo.label.error.load: the WebAssembly library could not be loaded.
topo.title: Spin a mesh
topo.lead: Colour shows the Gaussian curvature at each vertex. Invariants and curvature are computed by the project's C++ code, compiled to WebAssembly, in your browser.
topo.help: Drag to rotate, scroll or pinch to zoom; hover a point to read its curvature.
topo.label.nowebgl: Your browser cannot show 3D (WebGL unavailable); the invariants are still computed.
topo.label.error.invalid: invalid mesh (degenerate triangle or index out of range).
topo.note.boundary: On the boundary the angle defect measures how the boundary itself bends: boundary vertices take the colour of their interior neighbours.
